podcast.title: Burglary and Jail Sentence (July 25, 2003)
podcast.body: On July 25, 2003, after being kicked out of The Libertines, Pete Doherty retaliated by breaking into one of his bandmates' houses. He stole a guitar, a VCR, a computer, a harmonica, and a CD player, was quickly caught, and subsequently sentenced to six months in jail. "During one of the times he was kicked out of the band. This would be July 25, 2003. He broke into one of the band members' houses in retaliation for, of course, being kicked out of the band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Breakfast Challenge (2018)
podcast.body: In 2018, while reportedly clean and sober, Pete Doherty decided to undertake a breakfast challenge. He successfully consumed a massive meal consisting of four eggs, four strips of bacon, four sausages, an order of fries, hash browns, baked beans, mushrooms, "bubble and squeak" (a traditional dish of potato and cabbage fried together), and two thick slices of toast, completing the entire challenge in a swift 19 minutes and 30 seconds. "In 2018, supposedly clean and sober, he got hungry and decided to take on a breakfast challenge, where he ate four eggs, four strips of bacon, four sausages, an order of fries, hashbrowns, baked beans, mushrooms, something called bubble and squeak, which consists of potato and cabbage fried together, and two thick slices of toast."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Drug-Fueled Criminality and Animal Cruelty
podcast.body: Pete Doherty has a history marked by extensive drug abuse, involvement in "Grand Theft Auto," and at least one hit-and-run incident. He ignited widespread outrage among animal lovers when he was photographed attempting to get his cat to inhale something from a crack pipe. "Pete Dockardy of the British band Deliberteens, drugs, Grand Theft Auto, at least one hit and run, and he enraged animal lovers when he was pictured trying to get his cat to inhale something out of a crack pipe."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: In-and-Out Band/Rehab Status
podcast.body: Due to his ongoing drug issues, Pete Doherty has frequently been in and out of both the band and rehabilitation facilities. "He's been in and out of the band and in and out of rehab."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Living Room Gig "Job"
podcast.body: Pete Doherty has taken on a unique part-time job, charging 500 pounds to perform a gig in people's living rooms. "Pete has found himself a part-time job for 500 pounds who come and play a gig in your living room."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: London Revival Band
podcast.body: The Liberty's are cited as a Garage Rock revival band that came out of London, England, during the early 2000s. "The Liberty's came out of London, England."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Revivals Part 4: Garage Rock

podcast.title: Pete Doherty's Drug Addiction
podcast.body: Pete Doherty, a founding member, is noted for his "malevolent weirdness," predominantly fueled by a severe addiction to heroin and cocaine. He began using smack at 18 and, at one point, was injecting four or five times a day. "Pete is easily the freakyest member of the band and is prone to bouts of, well, let's call it malevolent weirdness, most of which are fueled by an addiction to heroin and cocaine."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Jail Drug Issue and Debt
podcast.body: Upon his release from jail, Pete Doherty continued to struggle with his drug addiction and also found himself 300,000 pounds in debt. "When he got out, he found that he still had a drug issue and he was 300,000 pounds in debt."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Shared Scene with Other Bands
podcast.body: The Libertines are described as being "cut from the same cloth" as other bands like The Vines, The Hives, The Strokes, The Datsuns, and The Doves, identifying them as part of the "raw indie rock scene." "The Liberty's are cut from the same cloth as the Vines, also the hives and the strokes and the datsums and the doves, you know, part of that whole raw indie rock scene."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Spiritual Advisor John "the Rabbi" Kahnmi
podcast.body: The Libertines have their own spiritual advisor named John Kahnmi. Despite being Catholic, he is referred to as "the Rabbi," is paid in alcohol, and is so popular with Libertines fans that he has his own Japanese fan club. "the Libertines have their own spiritual advisor. His name is John the Rabbi Kahnmi."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: The Good Mixer Regulars
podcast.body: The Libertines were among the bands who were regular patrons of The Good Mixer pub on Inverness Street in Camden, London, during the Britpop era of the early and mid-1990s. This pub was a key social spot where many groups of the era would gather. "Other regulars included the Librieteens and then later the darkness and travis."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.body: In January 2003, Lisa Moorish had a son, Astile Louis Dockerty, whose father is Pete Doherty, the singer of The Libertines. "January 2003, Lisa had a son, a steel, Louis Dockerty."

xref.title: Father of Astile Louis Dockerty
xref.body: Pete Doherty, known as the "famous drug-addled singer" of The Libertines and Babyshambles, is the father of Astile Louis Dockerty, born to Lisa Moorish in January 2003. "And before you ask, yes, the father is Pete Dockerty, the famous drug-addled singer of the Liberty's."
